claims.statement: Signals use a push-pull algorithm: writes eagerly push dirty state down the graph, while reads lazily pull and recompute only when an upstream dependency actually changed.

proof.quote: Signals use a push-pull algorithm: writes eagerly push dirty state down the graph, while reads lazily pull and recompute only when an upstream dependency actually changed.

claims.statement: Direct children of a changed source are marked Dirty, while transitive descendants are marked Check so they verify upstream versions before recomputing.

proof.quote: Direct children of a changed source are marked Dirty, while transitive descendants are marked Check so they verify upstream versions before recomputing.

claims.statement: Replacing per-node Set allocations with doubly-linked list nodes cuts memory overhead and allows O(1) subscription addition and stale edge pruning.
